{"body":"## Title\nAdd ability to duplicate rules\n\n## Summary\nWhen adding rules, you have to start from scratch each time. There are a number of different options to choose from in the dropdown menus, and it can be frustrating to remake rules that are the same or similar for multiple rules. When starting to use an app, People with very little patience would benefit from this feature.\n\n## User Story\nAs a very lazy person, I want to be able to duplicate rules so that I spend less time setting up my budgeting app.\n\n## User Scenario\nWhen creating rules, the user would have the option to select a pre-existing rule and click a button in the bottom right corner the says \"Duplicate.\" This would then bring up the Rule window with each option pre-filled in with the pre-existing rule's options. Then, the user could edit the rule as needed and save it.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. A button appears in the bottom right-hand corner when selecting a rule that says \"Duplicate.\"\n2. The Rule window appears and allows the user to edit the options.\n3. The new rule is saved, as well as the pre-existing rule not having been edited.\n4. The new rule exists between sessions with the options set.\n\n## Rough Scope\nMedium (4) - it requires a UI change as well as understanding how rules are created and saved in the code base.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Editing multiple rules at once\n- Adding new options for rules\n\n## Open Questions\n- Design decisions?\n- How would one ensure that the option is only available when one rule is selected?\n- How are rules created and saved in the code base?\n\n## Source\n- My own exploring","comments":[],"labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTldplM8AAAACzxR-iA","name":"scope: medium","description":"","color":"b5b323"}],"title":"Add ability to duplicate rules"}

46	export function mapValue(

60	  } else {

62	  }
63	  if (object) {
64	    return object.name;
65	  }
66	  return '(deleted)';
67	}

# Plan: Duplicate rules (issue #159)

## Context
Issue #159 asks for a way to duplicate a rule so users don't rebuild similar rules from scratch. Acceptance criteria:
1. A "Duplicate" button appears in the bottom-right of the Rules page when a rule is selected.
2. Clicking it opens the Rule editor pre-filled with the selected rule's options, editable.
3. Saving creates a **new** rule; the original is untouched.
4. The new rule persists across sessions.

## How rules work today (findings)
- [ManageRules.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/ManageRules.tsx) owns the Rules page. Selection comes from `useSelected('manage-rules', …)` (`selectedInst.items` is a `Set` of rule ids). The bottom-right footer (`SpaceBetween`, ~line 361) already shows "Delete N rules" when items are selected, plus "Create new rule".
- `onCreateRule()` builds a `NewRuleEntity` and opens the `edit-rule` modal via `pushModal`; `onEditRule()` does the same with an existing rule.
- [RuleEditor.tsx:1282-1327](packages/desktop-client/src/components/rules/RuleEditor.tsx#L1282-L1327) `onSave` picks `rule.id ? 'rule-update' : 'rule-add'`. So passing a rule **without `id`** saves a brand-new rule (persisted to SQLite via loot-core `rule-add`) — criteria 3 and 4 come for free.
- `RuleEntity = { id } & NewRuleEntity` ([rule.ts](packages/loot-core/src/types/models/rule.ts)).

## Approach
### 1. Helper to build the copy — `packages/desktop-client/src/util/rule.ts`
Add `export function duplicateRule(rule: RuleEntity): NewRuleEntity` that returns `{ stage, conditionsOp, conditions, actions }` with conditions/actions deep-cloned (`structuredClone`) and **no `id`/`tombstone`**, so the editor can't mutate the original and save goes through `rule-add`.

### 2. Duplicate button — `ManageRules.tsx`
- Compute `selectedRule` = the single rule in `allRules` matching `selectedInst.items` when `items.size === 1` (answers the issue's open question: only available with exactly one selection).
- Treat schedule-linked rules as not duplicable (`rule.actions.some(a => a.op === 'link-schedule')`): a copy would point a second rule at the same schedule. Hide the button for them.
- `onDuplicateSelected()`: `pushModal({ modal: { name: 'edit-rule', options: { rule: duplicateRule(selectedRule), onSave: async () => { await loadRules(); selectedInst.dispatch({ type: 'select-none' }); setLoading(false); } } } })` — same pattern as `onCreateRule`.
- Render `<Button onPress={onDuplicateSelected}><Trans>Duplicate</Trans></Button>` in the footer `SpaceBetween` next to "Delete N rules", so it sits bottom-right.

### 3. Tests
- **Unit**: `packages/desktop-client/src/util/rule.test.ts` (create or extend) — `duplicateRule` drops `id`, keeps stage/conditionsOp/conditions/actions equal, and returns new array/object references.
- **E2E**: in [rules-page.ts](packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/rules-page.ts) add `selectNthRule(index)` (click the row's select checkbox) and `duplicateSelectedRule()` returning an `EditRuleModal`. In [rules.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/e2e/rules.test.ts) add a test: create a rule → select it → Duplicate → change the action category → save → assert two rules exist, the original unchanged and the copy with the new category. No new screenshots (avoid VRT churn).

### 4. Housekeeping
- Release note `upcoming-release-notes/duplicate-rules.md` (use the writing-release-notes skill; category Features).
- `yarn generate:i18n` if the repo expects the new "Duplicate" string in the catalog.

## Verification
- `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix`, `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test` (unit test).
- `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run playwright test rules.test.ts --browser=chromium`.
- Manual: `yarn start` → "View demo" → Rules: select one rule → Duplicate appears; select two/zero or a schedule rule → it doesn't. Duplicate, edit, save → new rule shows up, original unchanged; reload page → the new rule is still there.

    if (data.conditions) {
      await this.fillEditorFields(data.conditions, this.conditionList, true);
    }

    if (data.actions) {
      await this.fillEditorFields(data.actions, this.actionList);
    }

    if (data.splits) {
      let idx = data.actions?.length ?? 0;
      for (const splitActions of data.splits) {
        await this.splitIntoMultipleTransactionsButton.click();
        await this.fillEditorFields(splitActions, this.actionList.nth(idx));
        idx++;
      }
    }
  }

  async fillEditorFields(
    data: Array<ConditionsEntry | ActionsEntry | SplitsEntry>,
    rootElement: Locator,
    fieldFirst = false,
  ) {
    for (const [idx, entry] of data.entries()) {
      const { field, op, value } = entry;

      const row = await this.getRow(rootElement, idx);

      if (!(await row.isVisible())) {
        await this.addEntry(rootElement);
      }

      if (op && !fieldFirst) {
        await this.selectOp(row, op);
      }

      if (field) {
        await this.selectField(row, field);
      }

      if (op && fieldFirst) {
        await this.selectOp(row, op);
      }

      if (value && value.length > 0) {
        const input = row.getByRole('textbox');
        const existingValue = await input.inputValue();
        if (existingValue) {
          await input.selectText();
        }
        // Using pressSequentially here to simulate user typing.
        // When using .fill(...), playwright just "pastes" the entire word onto the input
        // and for some reason this breaks the autocomplete highlighting logic
        // e.g. "Create payee" option is not being highlighted.
        await input.pressSequentially(value);
        await this.page.keyboard.press('Enter');
      }
    }
  }

  async selectConditionsOp(conditionsOp: string | RegExp) {
    await this.conditionsOpButton.click();

    const conditionsOpSelectOption =
      await this.getPopoverSelectOption(conditionsOp);
    await conditionsOpSelectOption.click();
  }

  async selectOp(row: Locator, op: string) {
    await row.getByTestId('op-select').getByRole('button').click();

    const opSelectOption = await this.getPopoverSelectOption(op);
    await opSelectOption.waitFor({ state: 'visible' });
    await opSelectOption.click();
  }

  async selectField(row: Locator, field: string) {
    await row.getByTestId('field-select').getByRole('button').click();

    const fieldSelectOption = await this.getPopoverSelectOption(field);
    await fieldSelectOption.waitFor({ state: 'visible' });
    await fieldSelectOption.click();
  }

  async getRow(locator: Locator, index: number) {
    return locator.getByTestId('editor-row').nth(index);
  }

  async addEntry(locator: Locator) {
    await locator.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add entry' }).click();
  }

  async getPopoverSelectOption(value: string | RegExp) {
    // Need to use page because popover is rendered outside of modal locator
    return this.page
      .locator('[data-popover]')
      .getByRole('button', { name: value, exact: true });
  }

  async save() {
    await this.saveButton.click();
  }

  async cancel() {
    await this.cancelButton.click();
  }

  async close() {
    await this.heading.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' }).click();
  }
}

import type { RuleEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { duplicateRule } from '#util/rule';

const rule: RuleEntity = {
  id: 'rule-1',
  stage: 'pre',
  conditionsOp: 'or',
  conditions: [{ field: 'payee', op: 'is', value: 'payee-1', type: 'id' }],
  actions: [{ op: 'set', field: 'category', value: 'cat-1', type: 'id' }],
};

describe('duplicateRule', () => {
  it('copies the rule options without its id', () => {
    const copy = duplicateRule(rule);

    expect(copy).not.toHaveProperty('id');
    expect(copy).toEqual({
      stage: 'pre',
      conditionsOp: 'or',
      conditions: rule.conditions,
      actions: rule.actions,
    });
  });

  it('does not share conditions or actions with the original', () => {
    const copy = duplicateRule(rule);

    expect(copy.conditions).not.toBe(rule.conditions);
    expect(copy.conditions[0]).not.toBe(rule.conditions[0]);
    expect(copy.actions).not.toBe(rule.actions);
    expect(copy.actions[0]).not.toBe(rule.actions[0]);
  });
});

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

I've added a "Duplicate" button for rules (issue #159). The new unit and e2e tests pass. I worked on a new branch, `feat/duplicate-rules`, made from `master`, so your `feat/attach-receipts` work isn't affected. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works**
- When exactly one rule is selected on the Rules page, a **Duplicate** button appears at the bottom right, next to "Delete N rules". This answers the issue's open question about allowing only one selected rule.
- Clicking it opens the usual rule editor, filled in with a copy of that rule's settings. Saving creates a new rule; the original isn't touched. The copy is saved like any other new rule, so it's still there after a reload.
- **One choice I made that isn't in the issue:** the button is hidden for rules that belong to a schedule. Copying one would link a second rule to the same schedule.

**Changes**
- [util/rule.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/util/rule.ts): a new `duplicateRule()` helper. It makes a full copy of the rule without its id, so editing the copy can't change the original.
- [ManageRules.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/ManageRules.tsx): the button and when it shows.
- Tests:
  - [util/rule.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/util/rule.test.ts) (new) checks the helper.
  - A new e2e test in [rules.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/e2e/rules.test.ts) covers the whole flow: create a rule, select it, duplicate it, change the category, save, then check both rules exist and are still there after a reload.
  - [rules-page.ts](packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/rules-page.ts) gets two small helpers for that test.
- Release note: [upcoming-release-notes/duplicate-rules.md](upcoming-release-notes/duplicate-rules.md).

**Checks run**
- `yarn typecheck` and oxlint pass, and the changed files are formatted.
- The e2e test failed on my first attempt: I didn't know the demo budget already has a schedule rule for the same payee, and the test clicked before the editor had closed. I fixed the test, and it now passes.
- I didn't run the rest of `rules.test.ts`, because its screenshot tests need the Linux Docker setup. The button only appears when a rule is selected, so the existing screenshots shouldn't change.

The feature works, and your code is up to date. You're on `feat/duplicate-rules` with all the changes in place, and the e2e test clicks the button in a real browser. Most likely the button was there but stayed hidden because of how I set it up. It only shows when **all** of these are true:

// Services

function onRuleUpdate(rule) {
  const { actions, conditions } =
    rule instanceof Rule ? rule.serialize() : ruleModel.toJS(rule);

  if (actions && actions.find(a => a.op === 'link-schedule')) {
    const scheduleId = actions.find(a => a.op === 'link-schedule').value;

    if (scheduleId) {
      const conds = extractScheduleConds(conditions);

      const payeeIdx = conditions.findIndex(c => c === conds.payee);
      const accountIdx = conditions.findIndex(c => c === conds.account);
      const amountIdx = conditions.findIndex(c => c === conds.amount);
      const dateIdx = conditions.findIndex(c => c === conds.date);

      db.runQuery(
        'INSERT OR REPLACE INTO schedules_json_paths (schedule_id, payee, account, amount, date) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)',
        [
          scheduleId,
          payeeIdx === -1 ? null : `$[${payeeIdx}]`,
          accountIdx === -1 ? null : `$[${accountIdx}]`,
          amountIdx === -1 ? null : `$[${amountIdx}]`,
          dateIdx === -1 ? null : `$[${dateIdx}]`,
        ],
      );
    }
  }
}

function trackJSONPaths() {
  // Populate the table
  db.transaction(() => {
    getRules().forEach(rule => {
      onRuleUpdate(rule);
      }
      return null;
    });

    return result.filter((res): res is string => typeof res === 'string').length
      ? result
      : null;
  }

  const conditionErrors = runValidation(
    rule.conditions,
    cond => new Condition(cond.op, cond.field, cond.value, cond.options),
  );

  const actionErrors = runValidation(rule.actions, action =>
    action.op === 'delete-transaction'
      ? new Action(action.op, null, null, null)
      : action.op === 'set-split-amount'
        ? new Action(action.op, null, action.value, action.options)
        : action.op === 'link-schedule'
          ? new Action(action.op, null, action.value, null)
          : action.op === 'prepend-notes' || action.op === 'append-notes'
            ? new Action(action.op, null, action.value, null)
            : new Action(action.op, action.field, action.value, action.options),
  );

  if (conditionErrors || actionErrors) {
    return {
      conditionErrors,
      actionErrors,
    };
  }

  return null;
}

type ValidationError = {
  conditionErrors: string[];
  actionErrors: string[];
};

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 19:08:21Z)**_

You can now duplicate rules that are linked to a schedule. The copy is a separate rule that isn't tied to the schedule.

**What happens when you duplicate a schedule rule**
- The copy keeps all of the rule's conditions: payee, account, date and amount.
- The "link schedule" action is removed from the copy. If that was the rule's only action, the copy gets a blank "set category" action instead, like "Create new rule" does, so you can pick what it should do.
- The original rule and its schedule aren't changed.

I left the schedule link out of the copy on purpose. When a rule that links to a schedule is saved, the server points the schedule at that rule's conditions ([schedules/app.ts:496-523](packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts#L496-L523)). A copy that kept the link would quietly take the schedule over from the original rule. If you'd rather have Duplicate make a new schedule as well, that's a bigger change, but I can look into it.

**Changes**
- [util/rule.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/util/rule.ts): `duplicateRule()` now removes the schedule link from the copy.

Base directory for this skill: c:\Users\reese\SE\actual-budget\.claude\skills\committing-actual-changes

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

## Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Why is it needed? Please give context on the "why?": why do we need this change? What problem is it solving for you?-->

Adds a **Duplicate** button to the Rules page. Until now, every new rule had to be built from scratch, even when it was almost the same as an existing one. Duplicate opens the rule editor already filled in with a copy of the selected rule. The user can change what they need and save it as a new rule, and the original rule is not changed.

Changes:

- **Duplicate button:** `ManageRules.tsx`. The button is always shown at the bottom right, next to "Create new rule". It is enabled only when exactly one rule is selected. When it's disabled, a tooltip says why: "Select a rule to duplicate" or "Select only one rule to duplicate".
- **Copying a rule:** `duplicateRule()` in `util/rule.ts`. It makes a full copy of the rule's stage, conditions and actions without the rule's `id`. Because there is no `id`, the editor saves the copy through `rule-add` as a new rule instead of updating the original with `rule-update` (`RuleEditor.tsx`, `onSave`).
- **Rules linked to schedules:** these can be duplicated too, but the copy does not keep the "link schedule" action. Saving a rule that links to a schedule points that schedule at the saved rule (`onRuleUpdate` in `loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts`), so a copy that kept the link would quietly take the schedule over from the original rule. The copy keeps all of the conditions. If the schedule link was its only action, it gets a blank "set category" action, the same one "Create new rule" starts with.
- **Tests:** 4 unit tests in `util/rule.test.ts` and 2 e2e tests in `e2e/rules.test.ts`. The `RulesPage` page model gets `selectNthRule()` and `duplicateSelectedRule()`.
- **Release note:** `upcoming-release-notes/duplicate-rules.md`.

No screenshots are added or changed. With no rule selected, the Rules page only gains a disabled button in the footer.

To get the CI result, you need to open a pull request. Your repo's CI only runs on pull requests and on pushes to `master`, not on pushes to other branches. That's why nothing has run on `feat/duplicate-rules` yet (`gh run list` shows no runs). The main checks, `check.yml`, `build.yml` and `e2e-test.yml`, are all set up this way.

**Steps**

1. **Open the PR.** If you don't want reviewers looking at it yet, open it as a **draft**: on GitHub use the arrow next to "Create pull request" → "Create draft pull request", or run `gh pr create --draft`. Opening it starts CI.
2. **Wait for the checks.** They appear at the bottom of the PR's Conversation tab and in its **Checks** tab. The e2e tests usually take the longest. In a terminal, `gh pr checks --watch` shows them live and finishes when they're all done.
3. **Fill in the TODO.** Edit the PR description and replace `CI result: [TODO]` with the outcome, e.g. "All checks pass in CI", or name any that failed.

**What to watch for**

- The two new e2e tests are in `rules.test.ts`, so they run in the **E2E tests** job.
- If a screenshot test fails there, start with the visual-regression report the e2e job uploads. This PR shouldn't change any screenshots, so any differences are worth a look.
